knowledge_graph.title: Rickettsia
knowledge_graph.description: Rickettsia is a genus of nonmotile, gram-negative, nonspore-forming, highly pleomorphic bacteria that may occur in the forms of cocci, bacilli, or threads. The genus was named after Howard Taylor Ricketts in honor of his pioneering work on tick-borne spotted fever.

text_blocks.snippet: Rickettsial infections are a group of diseases caused by bacteria called Rickettsia and Orientia, transmitted to humans through the bites of infected ticks, mites, fleas, or lice. These infections can cause a range of symptoms, including fever, headache, rash, and muscle aches, and in severe cases, can be life-threatening.
snippet_highlighted_words: a group of diseases caused by bacteria called Rickettsia and Orientia, transmitted to humans through the bites of infected ticks, mites, fleas, or lice

list.title: Causative agents:
list.snippet: Rickettsiae are obligate intracellular bacteria, meaning they can only survive and reproduce inside the cells of another organism.

list.title: Transmission:
list.snippet: Humans typically get infected through the bite of an infected arthropod vector.

list.title: Symptoms:
list.snippet: Common symptoms include fever, headache, rash, and a general feeling of illness. Some infections may also cause a black, scab-like sore (eschar) at the bite site, swollen lymph nodes, confusion, and severe weakness.

list.title: Severity:
list.snippet: While some rickettsial infections are mild, others like Rocky Mountain spotted fever, Mediterranean spotted fever, epidemic typhus, and scrub typhus can be severe and potentially fatal.

list.title: Examples:
list.snippet: Rocky Mountain spotted fever (caused by Rickettsia rickettsii), murine typhus (caused by Rickettsia typhi), and Rickettsialpox (caused by Rickettsia akari) are examples of rickettsial diseases.

list.title: Treatment:
list.snippet: Prompt antibiotic treatment, usually with doxycycline, is crucial for effective management.

list.title: Prevention:
list.snippet: Avoiding bites from ticks, mites, fleas, and lice is the primary way to prevent rickettsial infections. This includes wearing protective clothing, using insect repellent, and checking for and removing ticks promptly.
